# dsh-profile-gist-sync

Back up this DSH profile's configuration to an **unlisted secret GitHub Gist**,
pull it back on anot
her machine, and see at a glance whether the two agree.

A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)
plugin: a page in **Settings → Plugins → 配置同步 / Config sync**, and a
`con
fig_backup` tool for the agent.
页面位置：**设置 → 插件 → 配置同步**。Agent 侧工具：`config_backup`。
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then restart DSH. No dependencies, no build step, no install scripts: the
package is plain ESM that

. No dependencies, no build step, no install scripts: the
package is plain ESM that Node runs as-is.
## The page
Three numbered steps, one button each; nothing has to be typed.

1. **状态** — one line saying whether the cloud copy and this machine agree,
plus the profile, the fil

e count, and the last upload/sync. It checks the
cloud by itself on open; 重新检查 does it again.
2. **上

传** — 上传到云端 backs this machine up to the cloud. The Gist this
profile already uses is updated, and t

he first upload creates one and
remembers it. 另存为本地文件 writes the same backup to a local file instead

.
3. **同步** — 从云端同步 writes the cloud copy here, with 撤销上次同步 offered
afterwards.

Everything fiddly (the Gist id, a token, the machine-state checkbox, restoring
from a backup file, t

he file list) sits in a collapsed **高级设置** section. The
Gist id and the last upload/sync are remembe

red in
`<profile>/.dsh-config-sync/settings.json`; that file is never part of a backup.
## What leaves this machine
Short version, for anyone deciding whether to install this:

- The only host ever contacted is `api.github.com`. The checks in `test/` fail if
the plugin opens a

ny other connection.
- Upload sends text configuration only — the files listed below. Credential
sto

res, binaries, `node_modules`, the lockfile, and this machine's usage
counters are excluded, and the

UI names every exclusion instead of hiding it.
- The Gist is created `public: false`. **Unlisted, n

ot private**: anyone with the
link can read it, so the link is the secret.
- The GitHub token is nev

er written anywhere; it is used for one request and can
come from the request body, the host environ

ment, or a signed-in `gh` CLI.
- The Gist id lives in `<profile>/.dsh-config-sync/settings.json` — i

nside a
hidden directory, which backups never carry, so syncing a machine never leaks
the id of the

machine it came from.
- Restoring is merge-style and reversible: nothing is written before the
overw
ritten bytes are snapshotted for 撤销上次同步.
## What a backup carries

Text configuration from the profile directory: `package.json`,
`cordis.patch.yml`, `cordis.yml`, `.n

pmrc`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`,
`data/*.json`, `suppliers/*`, and any other text file the profile hold

s. The
document format is `dsh-profile-backup` v0.2 — the same one the DSH plugin market
reads and w
rites, so a backup from here imports there and vice versa.
Never included, and always listed as excluded in the UI:
| Path | Why |

| `node_modules/`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` | reproducible from `package.json` |
| `.git/`, `*.bak` | VCS st

ate and repair leftovers |
| hidden directories (`.dsh-market/`, `.plugin-manager/`, `.dsh-config-sy

nc/`) | logs, caches, this plugin's own undo snapshots |
| `data/auths/credentials.sqlite`, any othe

r binary file | a credential store, and not portable |
| `data/usage.json` | this machine's counters
— include with the checkbox when wanted |

A backup written elsewhere may still carry entries this plugin does not write
into a profile: the pl

ugin market's exporter, for example, includes
`data/auths/credentials.sqlite`. Importing such a docu

ment is not refused — the
credential store, cached binaries, backup copies, oversized files, and hid

den
directories are skipped, the rest of the configuration is restored, and the plan
lists exactly w

hat was ignored and why. Only a path that escapes the profile, a
dependency directory, a duplicate p

ath, a malformed entry, or a document with no
usable `package.json` is a hard refusal.
## Restore
Merge-style and reversible:

- Files in the backup are written; files only the local machine has stay.
- `package.json` is **merg

ed**: dependencies and `dsh.profile.bundles` are
unioned, so plugins already installed on the target

machine are kept.
- Every overwritten or created path is copied into
`<profile>/.dsh-config-sync/un

do/<stamp>/` first, so the import can be undone
from the page or with the tool's `undo` action.
- In

stalled plugins are not part of a backup: after a restore that adds
dependencies, install them from
the plugins page and restart DSH.
## GitHub Gist

Upload updates the Gist this profile remembers, or creates a secret one and
remembers it the first t

ime; leave the id empty in 高级设置 and save to start a
different Gist, or paste an id/link to adopt one

. Download reads
`dsh-profile-backup.json` from it and validates the document before anything is
wri

nload reads
`dsh-profile-backup.json` from it and validates the document before anything is
written.

The token is never stored: paste one per session, or set `DSH_GITHUB_TOKEN` /
`GITHUB_TOKEN` on the

host, or sign in with the `gh` CLI — the page offers a
"check token" button that reports which sourc

e answered. A secret Gist is
unlisted, **not private**: anyone with the link can read it.
## Agent tool

`config_backup` with `action`: `status`, `export`, `gist_upload`, `gist_read`,
`restore`, `undo`. Gi

st actions use the remembered cloud copy when `gistId` is
omitted, so "back this up" and "sync my co

nfiguration" work without an id.
`export` writes inside `<profile>/.dsh-config-sync/exports/`, and `

restore`
reads only from inside the DSH home directory, so the tool cannot be used as a
file-system

`
reads only from inside the DSH home directory, so the tool cannot be used as a
file-system escape.
## Checks
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Four check files, each a separate process, all offline: profiles are temporary
directories, the GitH

ub HTTP layer is stubbed (and refuses every host but
`api.github.com`), and the only server any chec

k talks to is its own loopback
port. They cover the document format and its exclusions, the restore

plan and
undo, the activation contract, the route and tool surface, the first-run journey
